stories.headline: US Iran War Highlights: Trump claims Tehran wants US to open Strait of Hormuz quickly
stories.summary: The US and Iran have reached a ceasefire deal after President Trump threatened to target Iran's civilization if commercial shipping was not allowed through the Strait of Hormuz. Iran's Revolutionary Guard stated that the strait would remain closed due to US ceasefire violations, and approaching vessels would be treated as "cooperating with the enemy". Despite the US claiming to have destroyed most of Iran's naval capabilities, Tehran still has smaller boats and anti-ship cruise missiles that could render the strait impassable. Iran has set three conditions to reopen the strait, which the US has not publicly accepted. A proposed two-week ceasefire has been agreed upon, conditional on shipping traffic being allowed to move through the strait. The situation remains tense, with the US and Iran having differing views on control of the strategic waterway. Trump has called for Iran to negotiate an end to the war.

stories.headline: Hezbollah drone strikes target Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon
stories.summary: Hezbollah launched drone strikes targeting Israeli soldiers in southern Lebanon, with multiple incidents reported in recent days. On Sunday, an Israeli soldier was killed and six others wounded in a drone attack. Another soldier was severely wounded in a similar incident on Monday. Hezbollah claimed responsibility for the attacks, stating that drones and rockets targeted Israeli soldiers and tanks in southern Lebanon and northern Israel. Israel has responded with airstrikes and interceptions of aerial targets. The violence has continued despite a fragile ceasefire, with Israel issuing new displacement orders for south Lebanon. The incidents have resulted in casualties on both sides, with the conflict showing no signs of easing. Israeli forces remain on high alert, and the situation remains volatile.

stories.headline: Sh100bn Kenya tea, flowers and meat exports stuck as Middle East conflict bites
stories.summary: Kenya's exports of tea, flowers, and meat to the Middle East are valued at Sh100bn and are currently stuck due to the ongoing conflict in the region. The US-Israel war with Iran has disrupted export markets, directly impacting Kenyan exporters. Other affected exports include meat, vegetables, coffee, and flowers. The crisis has also had a broader impact, pushing up energy prices and contributing to increased food costs in countries such as the UK. The conflict is having far-reaching effects, with Vietnam's economy also experiencing ripple effects due to tightened energy markets and disrupted sea-lanes. The situation is being closely monitored, with businesses warning of potential long-term consequences for global trade and economies. Kenya's exporters are among those feeling the pinch, with no clear resolution to the conflict in sight.

stories.headline: Bosnia signs up to Trump-linked pipeline to reduce Russian gas dependence
stories.summary: Bosnia and Herzegovina has approved a $1.5 billion energy project led by US company AAFS Infrastructure and Energy LLC, which has links to former US President Donald Trump. The project aims to reduce Bosnia's dependence on Russian natural gas by connecting the country to a liquefied natural gas terminal off the Croatian coast. This will allow US gas to reach Bosnia, which currently relies on Russia for its entire gas supply. The European Union has warned that the deal could jeopardize Bosnia's bid to join the bloc. The pipeline project is expected to decrease Bosnia's reliance on Russian gas, with US gas set to become a new source of energy for the country. The move is seen as a strategic effort to diversify Bosnia's energy sources and reduce its dependence on Russia.

stories.headline: Denuvo Has Been Fully Cracked And 2K Is Fighting Back Using a relatively new bypass technique, hackers claim to have effectively cracked all games using Denuvo protection software
stories.summary: Hackers have cracked Denuvo protection software using a relatively new bypass technique, allowing them to effectively crack all games previously protected by it. This includes single-player games, rendering Denuvo's protection useless. In response, 2K Games and Denuvo have implemented mandatory 14-day online checks for some games. The bypass technique, known as the hypervisor bypass, requires users to disable Virtualization-Based Security (VBS) to work. Denuvo has been criticized in the past for potentially degrading game performance due to increased CPU utilization, a claim the company has denied. The crack has significant implications for game developers and publishers, who may need to explore alternative protection methods to prevent piracy. The move to online DRM checks is seen as a retaliation against the crack, aiming to limit piracy and protect game sales.

stories.headline: Nvidia Is Finally Doing Something About the RAM Apocalypse Hopefully, it’s the start of better, more affordable GPU options.
stories.summary: Nvidia is addressing the RAM shortage by offering a new laptop GPU, the GeForce RTX 5070, with 12GB of RAM. This mobile GPU will be available to manufacturers this year, potentially leading to a new batch of laptops with improved performance. The move comes after months of Nvidia's RTX 50-series graphics cards being affected by the RAM crisis. Meanwhile, AMD's Radeon RX 9070 offers an alternative with more VRAM and higher performance, without significant price increases. The global RAM shortage has previously led to reports of Nvidia potentially cutting GPU production in 2026. The new RTX 5070 GPU may provide a more affordable option for laptop buyers, although it remains to be seen how manufacturers will price these new laptops. The development is a response to the ongoing RAM shortage affecting the graphics card industry.

stories.headline: Critical GitHub.com and Enterprise Server RCE Vulnerability Enables Full Server Compromise A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-3854 in GitHub's internal git infrastructure that could have allowed any authenticated
stories.summary: A critical remote code execution (RCE) vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-3854, was discovered in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. The vulnerability could have allowed any authenticated user to compromise backend servers, access private repositories, and potentially achieve full server takeover, especially in GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) instances. The issue was reported by Google-owned cloud security firm Wiz on March 4, 2026, and GitHub validated and deployed a fix to GitHub.com within two hours. GitHub Enterprise Server users are advised to upgrade to version 3.19.3 or later to patch the vulnerability. Patches are available for all supported releases, and users are strongly recommended to upgrade immediately to prevent potential exploitation. The fix is already in place for GitHub.com users, who do not need to take any action.

stories.headline: Lidl owners try to lure German politicians with ‘middle-aisle offer’ of a secure messaging app Bundestag lobbied by owners of supermarket chain after dozens of chat groups were hacked, exposing some messages by chancellor Friedrich Merz
stories.summary: The owners of Lidl, a German supermarket chain, are lobbying the Bundestag to adopt a secure messaging app after dozens of chat groups were hacked, exposing messages from politicians, including Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The hacking occurred after a phishing scam, in which victims were tricked into revealing sensitive account information, allowing hackers to access chat groups, messages, photos, and files. The scam involved fake Signal support messages asking users to enter a PIN, open a link, or scan a QR code. European cybersecurity agencies had warned of a similar phishing campaign by Russian hackers in early April, and Germany's domestic intelligence service had issued a warning in February. The Lidl owners' proposal aims to provide a secure alternative for German politicians to communicate. The incident has raised concerns about the security of communication among German politicians.

stories.headline: Chelsea trio including Enzo Fernandez hang out with Jude Bellingham at Madrid Open after star flirted with transfer
stories.summary: Chelsea midfielder Enzo Fernandez was spotted in Madrid at the Madrid Open, where he met up with Jude Bellingham. This comes after Fernandez was disciplined by Chelsea for flirting with a potential transfer to Real Madrid. Fernandez, an Argentine professional footballer, plays for both Chelsea and the Argentina national team. He was joined by two other Chelsea players at the event. The sighting has sparked interest given the recent transfer speculation surrounding Fernandez and Real Madrid. Fernandez's versatility on the field, playing as a central, defensive, or attacking midfielder, has made him a valuable asset to Chelsea. The meeting with Bellingham, a prominent footballer, has added to the buzz around Fernandez's future with Chelsea.

stories.headline: The 'Temple of Speed', the Autodromo Nazionale Monza, Achieves Top 3-Star FIA Road Safety Rating
stories.summary: The Autodromo Nazionale Monza, also known as the 'Temple of Speed', has achieved a top 3-star FIA Road Safety Rating. The 5.793 km race track in Italy, built in 1922, is the oldest purpose-built motor racing circuit in mainland Europe. Supported by the Automobile Club d'Italia, Monza becomes the second racetrack in the world to receive this distinction. The FIA Road Safety Index's highest rating recognizes the circuit's commitment to road safety and responsible mobility. With this achievement, the Autodromo Nazionale Monza sets a global standard for road safety, solidifying its reputation as a leader in the motorsport industry. The 3-star rating is a testament to the circuit's dedication to providing a safe environment for drivers, spectators, and the community. This recognition further establishes Monza as a premier racing destination.

stories.headline: Why is Hardik of MI so different from Hardik of India?
stories.summary: Hardik Pandya's performance for Mumbai Indians (MI) has been underwhelming this season, contrasting with his significant contributions for the Indian national team. Former MI coach has defended Hardik, stating he should not be made a scapegoat. In a recent match against Lucknow Super Giants, Hardik missed an opportunity to score, leaving MI with an impossible task of 14 runs off 2 balls, resulting in a 12-run loss. Under Hardik's leadership, MI has shown glimpses of brilliance but lacks consistency. The team is aware of the formula for success in the Indian Premier League, which requires consistent performance throughout the tournament. Hardik also missed a match against Delhi Capitals, with MI making multiple changes to their side. His inconsistent form for MI continues to be a topic of discussion.

stories.headline: John Obi Mikel explains why Chelsea should not hire Cesc Fabregas
stories.summary: John Obi Mikel advises Chelsea against hiring Cesc Fabregas as their next manager, despite his success with Como. Mikel believes Fabregas needs more experience and suggests giving him a couple more seasons to establish himself. Instead, he recommends another ex-teammate, Filipe Luís, as a better option to take over at the club. Mikel's comments come after he criticized Chelsea's ownership for driving the team into chaos with constant managerial changes and instability. He also expressed concerns about the club's decision to part ways with manager Mauricio Pochettino's assistant, Mauricio Maresca, on New Year's Day, which he thinks will be regretted by owners Todd Boehly and Behdad Eghbali. Mikel's assessment highlights the uncertainty and turmoil surrounding Chelsea's managerial situation.

stories.headline: Election 2026 LIVE: Bengal heads for Phase 2 vote, Mamata Banerjee among over 1,000 candidates in fray
stories.summary: West Bengal is set to vote in the second phase of assembly polls, covering 142 seats and over 3.22 crore eligible voters. Chief Minister Mamata Banerjee is among over 1,000 candidates in the fray, contesting from the Bhabanipur constituency. She will face off against BJP's Leader of the Opposition Suvendu Adhikari in a high-profile battle. Voting began at 7 a.m. and will conclude later in the day. The second phase of polling is crucial, with several key constituencies going to the polls. The outcome will be significant in determining the state's political landscape. Over 3.22 crore voters are eligible to exercise their franchise in this phase, making it a pivotal moment in the West Bengal elections. The results of this phase will be closely watched, given the prominent candidates and constituencies involved.

stories.headline: The Hindu Odisha acts fast after tribal man carries sister’s remains to bank
stories.summary: A tribal man in Odisha carried his sister's skeletal remains to a bank to claim her savings, sparking outrage. The man was unable to navigate formal procedures to access the money in his late sister's account. The bank initially refused to process the claim, but later settled it after the man produced the required death certificate. The bank claimed the individual was inebriated when he first arrived and later returned with the human remains, creating a distressing situation. Police were immediately alerted, and the situation was handled. The incident highlights the difficulties faced by some individuals in accessing formal systems and the desperate measures they may take as a result. The bank has since processed the claim, and the matter has been resolved. An investigation into the incident is ongoing.

stories.headline: Biryani Dinner, Late-Night Watermelon, Then 4 Deaths: What Happened In Mumbai’s Bhendi Bazaar
stories.summary: Four members of a Mumbai family died after falling ill overnight following a dinner of biryani and late-night watermelon in the Bhendi Bazaar area. The family members consumed the meal and then ate watermelon, but soon fell severely ill. Despite efforts to save them, all four died within 12 hours. Investigators are awaiting postmortem findings to determine the cause of death, but food poisoning is suspected. The incident has left residents and doctors searching for answers, with the exact cause of the poisoning still unknown. The Mumbai police are investigating the matter, and the postmortem report is expected to provide more clarity on the circumstances surrounding the deaths. The tragedy has raised questions about the safety of the food consumed by the family.

stories.headline: Senior advocates to represent death row convicts: Supreme Court lays down directions for death penalty cases
stories.summary: The Supreme Court has laid down directions for death penalty cases, mandating trial courts to call for reports on aggravating and mitigating circumstances immediately after conviction and before sentencing. The court has also ordered that a dedicated legal team, consisting of one Senior Counsel and two advocates, must represent convicts in death sentence confirmation cases. This direction aims to ensure effective representation for death row convicts. The court's order comes in the context of the December 2012 gangrape and murder case in New Delhi, where two senior advocates have been appointed to defend the four death row convicts. The new norms, however, will not be applicable to all pending cases, and analysts note that while the court has not abolished the death penalty, it has effectively made it a rare event through these directions.

stories.headline: UAE exits Opec: What it means for global oil markets, Saudi influence, and energy geopolitics
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has confirmed its exit from OPEC and OPEC+ effective May 1, 2026, ending nearly six decades of membership. This move marks a significant shift in the UAE's energy diplomacy and may lead to greater turbulence in global energy markets. The UAE's departure could weaken coordinated oil supply management globally, potentially impacting oil prices and production. As a major oil producer, the UAE's exit may also reduce OPEC's influence and alter the dynamics between OPEC member countries, including Saudi Arabia. The UAE's decision could have far-reaching implications for global oil markets, with some estimates suggesting it could affect up to 40% of global crude production. The exit may also have significant implications for other OPEC member countries, including Nigeria, and the global energy landscape.

stories.headline: UAE quits OPEC, OPEC+ in major blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its departure from the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) and OPEC+, effective May 1. The move is a significant blow to the global oil producers' group, coming at a time of turmoil in the oil market due to the Iran war. The UAE cited energy strategy considerations as the reason for its departure. This decision could potentially allow the UAE to increase its oil and gas production. The departure exposes splits among Gulf nations and may have significant implications for the global oil market. The UAE's exit from OPEC and OPEC+, which includes allies like Russia, marks a major shift in the dynamics of the global oil industry. The move is expected to have far-reaching consequences for the oil market and the global economy.

stories.headline: UPDATE 1-UAE leaves OPEC and OPEC+ in major blow to global oil producers' group
stories.summary: The United Arab Emirates (UAE) has announced its withdrawal from OPEC and OPEC+, effective May 1, after nearly 60 years of membership. This move deals a significant blow to the oil producers' group, which is already facing an unprecedented energy crisis due to the Iran war. The UAE cited its decision to meet growing global energy demand in the long term. The country's exit from OPEC and OPEC+ is expected to impact global energy markets, which are currently contending with the biggest supply crisis in history. Oil prices trimmed gains on international markets following the announcement. The UAE's withdrawal is seen as a discord among Gulf nations, with Saudi Arabia, the de facto leader of OPEC, likely to be heavily affected by the decision. The move marks a significant shift in the global oil production landscape.

stories.headline: Don’t expect good news from central banks
stories.summary: Central banks around the world, including the Bank of Japan and European Central Bank (ECB), have been making headlines with their latest meetings and announcements. The Bank of Japan has already met, and the remaining central banks meeting this week are not expected to change interest rates. However, the outlook for most is becoming increasingly uncertain due to rising geopolitical tensions. The Federal Reserve, Bank of England, and other major central banks are also being closely watched for their responses to global economic developments. Currency and monetary policy, regulation, and market trends are all being impacted by central bank decisions. As the global economy navigates uncertain times, central banks are under scrutiny for their role in shaping the economic landscape. Their policies and announcements are being closely monitored for signs of change or stability.

stories.headline: Oil Price Surge, FII Outflows Drag Indian Stock Markets Lower Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty experienced declines due to a sharp rally in crude oil prices, continuous foreign fund outflows, and geopolitical uncertainty
stories.summary: Indian benchmark indices Sensex and Nifty declined due to a sharp rally in crude oil prices and persistent foreign fund outflows. The 30-share BSE Sensex fell 208.84 points to 77,094.79 in opening trade on Tuesday. The decline was driven by surging global crude oil prices, which unsettled investors. Continuous outflows by Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) also contributed to the downturn, reflecting fragile market sentiment influenced by external factors. Geopolitical uncertainty added to the pressure on the market. The decline in Sensex and Nifty was a result of these combined factors, which weakened investor confidence and impacted the banking sector. The Indian stock markets have been experiencing declines amid these external pressures, with oil price surges and foreign fund outflows being key contributors to the downward trend.

stories.headline: Market Wrap: Sensex slips 417 pts, Nifty closes below 24,000 as fading peace hopes and surging oil prices spook investors Indian stock markets, Sensex and Nifty, experienced a decline of up to 0.5% on Tuesday, reversing gains from the previous day
stories.summary: Indian stock markets, Sensex and Nifty, declined up to 0.5% on Tuesday, reversing previous day's gains. The downturn was triggered by renewed concerns over the US-Iran conflict, which fueled a surge in oil prices. Sensex fell 417 points to settle near 76,800, while Nifty 50 slipped below 24,000. Among Sensex constituents, Kotak Mahindra Bank slipped 4.41%, Mahindra & Mahindra declined 4.09%, and other major stocks such as Maruti Suzuki and IndiGo also saw declines. The market action indicates a range-bound movement with a weak bias, although the short-term uptrend status remains intact. Nifty formed a higher bottom at 23,813 on April 24. The decline was driven by high oil prices and weak global sentiment, weighing on investor confidence.

stories.headline: Stock market today (March 28, 2026): Which are the top gainers and losers in Nifty50 and BSE Sensex today? Check list India Business News: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended lower on Tuesday as rising crude oil prices and continued foreign fund outflows weakened
stories.summary: Benchmark equity indices Sensex and Nifty ended lower on March 28, 2026, due to rising crude oil prices and continued foreign fund outflows. The Nifty50 index, which tracks the top 50 stocks on the National Stock Exchange (NSE), and the Sensex, which tracks 30 leading companies on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), were affected. Crude oil prices are fluctuating, with Brent crude projected to trade between $96 and $103 per barrel. The stock market performance is crucial for gauging India's economic health. The Nifty and Sensex are key indicators of the country's stock market sentiment. On a different day, the indices pared most of their intra-day gains but still ended nearly half a percent higher, supported by strong buying in IT, PSU bank, and metal stocks. The stock exchanges will reopen on April 27, 2026.

stories.headline: Top Gainers & Losers on April 28: Tata Tech, Canara Bank, Maruti Suzuki, IndiGo, Axis Bank, Thermax among top losers On April 28, the Indian stock market resumed its downtrend, with the Nifty 50 and Sensex declining
stories.summary: The Indian stock market declined on April 28, with the Nifty 50 closing 0.40% lower at 23,995 and the S&P BSE Sensex down 0.54% at 76,886. Top losers included Axis Bank, Maruti Suzuki, and HCL Tech, which fell 2.5%, while ONGC gained 6%. Other losers were Shriram Finance, UltraTech Cement, and Infosys. The decline was attributed to a sell-off in PSU Bank stocks and surging global oil prices, which dampened investor sentiment. The Nifty Private Bank index also saw significant losses, with Axis Bank and Eternal declining nearly 2% and 3%, respectively. The market's downturn was reflected in the Sensex's 200-point slip, with SBI and IndiGo among the top losers. Overall, the market's negative trend was driven by a combination of global and domestic factors.

stories.headline: American Airlines CEO Rejects United Merger, Hints At Alaska Deal
stories.summary: American Airlines CEO Robert Isom has rejected a potential merger with United Airlines, calling it "a nonstarter from the get-go" due to anti-competitive concerns. Isom pledged to defend American's Chicago hub and expressed interest in exploring partnerships for growth, including a deeper tie with Alaska Airlines. He also mentioned the possibility of acquiring select assets from Spirit Airlines. The rejection comes after United Airlines CEO Scott Kirby reportedly pitched the merger idea to a Trump administration official, which was swiftly met with disapproval from all sides. Isom's comments signal a focus on strategic partnerships rather than large-scale mergers for American Airlines' future growth. The CEO's stance aims to protect the airline's interests and maintain its competitive position in the market.

stories.headline: Nigeria's oil output hits 5-year high as production reaches 1.71 million bpd
stories.summary: Nigeria's crude oil production has reached 1.71 million barrels per day, its highest level in five years. The Nigerian National Petroleum Company (NNPC) reported this growth, attributing it to upstream improvements, infrastructure upgrades, and sustained gas output of 7.5 billion standard cubic feet per day. The production increase was recorded between April 2025 and April 2026. Prior to this, Nigeria had seen a 10% increase in oil production to 1.71 million barrels per day in July, compared to the same period the previous year, according to the Nigerian Petroleum Refining Regulatory Commission. The country's oil output has been steadily rising, with the NNPC citing improvements in infrastructure and operations as key factors contributing to the growth. This milestone marks a significant increase in Nigeria's oil production, reaching its highest level in five years.

stories.headline: Phillips 66 completes sale of Lindsey Oil Refinery
stories.summary: Phillips 66 Limited has completed the acquisition of the assets and associated infrastructure of Prax Lindsey Oil Refinery Limited. The transaction follows an agreement made in January to integrate key assets into its Humber Refinery operations. The Lindsey Oil Refinery, located in North Lincolnshire, was previously owned by Prax Group, which went into administration, resulting in nearly 200 workers being made redundant. The Official Receiver took over the refinery in June 2025. Phillips 66 has now finalized the purchase, allowing the company to expand its operations and integrate the refinery's assets into its existing Humber Refinery. The completion of the sale marks a significant development for Phillips 66 and the future of the Lindsey Oil Refinery site.

stories.headline: Household real consumption per capita grows in both the euro area and the EU
stories.summary: In the fourth quarter of 2025, household real consumption per capita increased by 0.5% in the euro area and 0.6% in the EU. Household real income per capita rose by 0.1% in the euro area and 0.2% in the EU. The increase in household real income was mainly driven by net property income and other net current transfers in the euro area, and compensation of employees in the EU. The household saving rate decreased by 0.4 percentage points in the euro area and 0.5 percentage points in the EU, while the investment rate increased by 0.1 percentage point in both areas. These figures are based on seasonally adjusted quarterly European sector accounts published by Eurostat, the statistical office of the European Union.
